newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Perky New Zealand dollar closes near its highs.
newsitem.headline: Perky New Zealand dollar closes near its highs.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed near its highs on Wednesday after a busy session of good two-way business.
Dealers said it may be poised to test eight-year highs again if offshore demand persisted and while it received support from the Australian dollar.
At 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT), the Kiwi was at US$0.6959/66 compared with its 0.6946/53 opening. The Trade-Weighted Index finished at 65.95, well up on its 65.71 opening.
Dealers said the Kiwi had initially sunk to 0.6930 as longs were squeezed but the fall to that level attracted renewed buying. There were also rumours of bond-related activity.
"With the Aussie up around 80 (US) cents it's easy to play the Kiwi from the long side," said an Auckland dealer. "With the longs squeezed out, we may test 70 cents."

The market is picked to trade relatively quietly ahead of the Treasury's pre-election economic and fiscal update on Thursday and then, more importantly, the Reserve Bank's six-monthly economic projections on Friday morning.
Economists universally expect the RB to formally hold the line on monetary policy but some dealers expect the body language to indicate the market may be able to take interest rates lower.
If that is the case, the Kiwi could ease back, dealers said.
